stops.title: Homogeneous equation of degree 2 & angle between lines
stops.inShort: ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 represents two lines through the origin if h² − ab ≥ 0. Slopes m₁ + m₂ = −2h/b, m₁m₂ = a/b. Acute angle: tan θ = |2√(h² − ab) / (a + b)|. Perpendicular if a + b = 0; coincident if h² = ab.

stops.title: General second degree equation
stops.inShort: ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 represents a pair of lines if Δ = abc + 2fgh − af² − bg² − ch² = 0 and h² − ab ≥ 0.
sections: 4.4 General Second Degree Equation in x and y

items.s: Perpendicular if a + b = 0; coincident/parallel if h² = ab.

board.text: Prove that the acute angle θ between the lines represented by ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 is given by tan θ = |2√(h² − ab) / (a + b)| (a + b ≠ 0).
board.answer:
Let m₁, m₂ be slopes of the two lines. Then m₁ + m₂ = −2h/b and m₁m₂ = a/b.
(m₁ − m₂)² = (m₁ + m₂)² − 4m₁m₂ = 4h²/b² − 4a/b = 4(h² − ab)/b².
|m₁ − m₂| = 2√(h² − ab)/|b|.
tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| = |2√(h² − ab)/(a + b)|.

points.text: Sum and product of slopes m₁+m₂ = −2h/b, m₁m₂ = a/b

board.text: Find the joint equation of the pair of lines passing through the origin and perpendicular to the lines 5x² − 8xy + 3y² = 0.
board.answer:
5x² − 8xy + 3y² = (5x − 3y)(x − y) = 0.
Slopes are 5/3 and 1. Slopes of perpendicular lines are −3/5 and −1.
Equations: 3x + 5y = 0 and x + y = 0.
Joint equation: (3x + 5y)(x + y) = 3x² + 8xy + 5y² = 0.
